openings.claim: Does updating every book move improve complete pickup time once the sole clerk's update work and resulting waiting are counted? The synthetic packet establishes neither spare service capacity nor net benefit.
openings.delta: Make the live-update dependency testable against a location-freeze policy, separating address accuracy, maintenance work, waiting, and handoff time.
openings.prediction: If live maintenance consumes scarce peak capacity, current addresses reduce second searches but update work increases waiting; a feasible location freeze produces faster complete pickups.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is that avoided repeat searches save more clerk time than updates consume: live updating improves complete pickup time, including at peak load, over a feasible freeze.
openings.defeat: Comparable evening trials show live updates improve complete pickup time without extra staffing, preparation above ten minutes, identity exposure, or wrong-reader handoffs; this defeats the proposed maintenance bottleneck.
openings.probe: Propose matched evening windows using live updates and frozen verified exception locations. Record anonymous arrival, service-start, handoff, update time, second searches, arrival volume, and cart occupancy on existing paper. Only the existing clerk handles books. Keep identities behind the desk and use existing ownership verification if adequate. Reject either arm if preparation exceeds ten minutes or existing furniture cannot accommodate it. Compare the 95% two-minute target and wrong-reader handoffs; unmatched windows remain inconclusive. No trial has occurred.
assumptions: Fit concerns this proposed comparison; neither intervention is proven.
Comparable windows, adequate existing ownership verification, cart capacity, and clerk recording capacity are unconfirmed.
Pickup timing begins at arrival; if the stipulated measure differs, report waiting separately.

critiques.issue: Recording every move depends on service capacity that O5 and O6 leave unresolved. Fewer second searches alone cannot establish faster complete pickups. Q1 constructs a distinguishing comparison with the freeze alternative; its feasibility and outcomes remain unknown.
